sources.title: Original T5 release README
sources.evidence: The October 23, 2019 repository revision explicitly says the pretrained checkpoints have been released and links the exact large checkpoint directory. It names T5-Large with a nominal 770 million parameters, distinct from Base, 3B and 11B. Freshly reopened the original raw release README on October 27; the nominal 770M Large identity is unchanged.

sources.title: Original T5 release commit
sources.evidence: The commit containing the release README is timestamped 2019-10-23T23:52:05Z. The contemporaneous README already links the released Large weights; this is stronger evidence than a later model-host upload timestamp.

sources.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
sources.evidence: First submitted October 23, 2019; the paper states models and code are released. Read the full current PDF: section 3.7 describes Large as a dense encoder-decoder Transformer with 24 layers in each stack, width 1024, FFN width 4096, head dimension 64 and 16 heads. Section 2.1 describes tied input/output embeddings and relative position biases; 512-token sequences are an experimental training setup, not a stated architectural ceiling. The approximately 770M figure is nominal.

sources.title: Original Google T5-Large TensorFlow checkpoint index
sources.evidence: Downloaded only the 20,702-byte checkpoint index, not weight shards. Parsed original variable names/shapes: 509 BF16 model tensors total 737,668,096 parameters after excluding Adafactor optimizer slots and global_step. Encoder 302,040,576; decoder 402,728,448; shared embedding 32,899,072. One shared embedding and two self-attention relative-bias tables; no cross-attention relative-bias parameter. Shape products match BF16 byte sizes and independently derived architecture count.

sources.title: Original T5-Large operative configuration
sources.evidence: The released Large configuration specifies d_model=1024, d_ff=4096, d_kv=64, num_heads=16 and 24 layers per stack. Bitransformer.shared_embedding and shared_embedding_and_softmax_weights are true. Inputs and targets are configured to 512 tokens for this training run. This identifies the original T5 Large checkpoint, not T5 v1.1 or Flan. Freshly fetched and read the exact operative configuration on October 27; its 24-layer stacks, width, ReLU layers and tied embeddings still identify the original released architecture.

sources.title: Pinned T5-Large converted configuration
sources.evidence: Configuration identifies T5ForConditionalGeneration, is_encoder_decoder=true, vocabulary 32128 and the same Large dimensions as the original operative config. n_positions=512 is a saved default; there is no learned absolute-position table establishing a fixed maximum.

sources.title: Pinned converted T5-Large safetensors header
sources.evidence: Fetched only HTTP 206 ranges 0-7 and 8-62297. The 62,290-byte JSON header contains 510 F32 tensors totaling 737,668,608 stored elements, including an extra 512-element decoder cross-attention relative-bias table absent from the original checkpoint. Removing that unused conversion tensor gives exactly 737,668,096. Tied shared embedding appears once; no packed quantization tensors or optimizer state in this file.

sources.title: Pinned T5 implementation
sources.evidence: T5ForConditionalGeneration explicitly ignores decoder.block.0.layer.1.EncDecAttention.relative_attention_bias.weight on load, and cross-attention is constructed with has_relative_attention_bias=False. Encoder input, decoder input and output head tie to shared.weight. Relative-distance buckets accept variable sequence lengths; their maximum-distance bucket is not a context-length ceiling.

sources.title: Pinned T5 Large model card
sources.evidence: The exact Large card attributes the model to the original T5 authors, declares Apache 2.0, describes text-to-text tasks and reiterates nominal 770M. It describes a mixture of denoising and supervised text tasks. It provides no dedicated thinking, tool-calling, inference-active parameter count or fixed maximum-context specification. Freshly retrieved the complete pinned raw card on October 27; it still states 770 million total parameters and supplies no separate active count.

sources.title: Original T5 Apache License 2.0
sources.evidence: The original release repository carries Apache License 2.0. The exact converted checkpoint card independently declares the same model license.

sources.title: Later Google T5 research: Distilling step-by-step
sources.evidence: September 2023 article and linked research discuss a 770M T5 model and downstream rationale training. They do not disclose an original T5-Large per-token inference-active count; capabilities acquired by later distillation are not attributed to the original checkpoint.

sources.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, Appendix D
sources.evidence: Later paper Table D.1 labels T5-Large as 770M with 0.5 fraction of parameters active per token for an approximate training-compute calculation. The appendix explicitly simplifies away attention costs. This is not a Google-disclosed inference-active parameter count and is not multiplied into the catalog field.

sources.title: Original T5 JMLR paper, section 3.7
sources.evidence: Read the full paper from the October 27 fresh primary-source cache. Section 3.7 specifies the original Large dimensions and approximately 770M total parameters. Neither the model-size discussion nor the comparisons define a separate Large active-parameter convention. This corroborates the nominal label without replacing the previously verified exact total.

sources.title: BMCook: A Task-agnostic Compression Toolkit for Big Models
sources.evidence: Freshly read the original paper, especially section 3 and Table 2. The T5-Large baseline is labeled 0.60GB Activated Model Size. The authors explicitly define that metric from attention and FFN layers, exclude embeddings, and reduce it fourfold under eight-bit quantization. It is a byte-size theoretical-compute proxy, not a published total number of active parameters; converting it into a whole-model active count would add an unsupported convention.

sources.title: Alternating updates for efficient transformers
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened Google’s November 7, 2023 original research post and its linked paper arxiv.org/html/2301.13310v2. The 770M T5-Large figure is total size. AltUp changes representations and updates, while conditional-activation discussion concerns its altered models; no separate active count for the original T5-Large checkpoint is published.

sources.title: MoEfication: Transformer Feed-forward Layers are Mixtures of Experts
sources.evidence: Freshly inspected the original study. Its T5-Large example measures the fraction of FFN neurons with positive ReLU outputs, and its converted MoE models use selected FFN experts. Those activation ratios and changed routing do not establish a separately published whole-model parameter count for original dense T5-Large.

sources.title: Entities: what are they, where are they and how do we model them?
sources.publisher: Daniel M. Bikel / Google Research / NIST TAC
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened the original presentation and visually inspected slide 74. Its All and Activated parameter columns identify T5 3B and T5 11B, including a separate 11B salient-span-masking row. T5-Large is absent. This valid comparison convention cannot be transferred to an unlisted differently sized sibling.

sources.title: Official Flan-T5-Large configuration
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched original Google configuration after the MTEB Flan-Large profile surfaced a 750M active figure. Flan-Large uses gated-GELU, d_ff=2816 and untied output embeddings, whereas original Large uses ReLU, d_ff=4096 and tied embeddings. It is not an unchanged original-Large fine-tune, so its parameter figures cannot be inherited.

name.note: Normalize the original T5-Large variant name; not T5 v1.1 Large, Flan-T5 Large or a task-specific derivative.

developer.note: The original paper and release are from Google Research.

release_date.note: Retain the dated original release README and same-day paper release. The February 2020 Google blog is later publicity, not the first release.

open_weights.note: Original Google weights are released publicly; exact original index and converted checkpoint header are accessible without authentication.

license.note: Original repository license and exact model-card license agree.

parameters_b.note: Exact unique full-model count: 737,668,096 = encoder 302,040,576 + decoder 402,728,448 + shared embedding 32,899,072. Original checkpoint index excludes optimizer slots and global_step; all 509 model tensors are BF16. Independent shape formula with both 24-layer stacks, feed-forward and attention matrices, normalization vectors and two relative-bias tables agrees. Tied encoder/decoder input and output embedding counted once. Converted HF storage adds an unused 512-element cross-attention bias, explicitly ignored by the implementation. The published 770M label is approximate and is not treated as the exact unique count. No weight shards were downloaded. October 27 re-audit freshly confirms the nominal 770M label and exact released configuration. Retain the existing supported 737,668,096 total; no tensor census or weight download was repeated.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-model active/activated searches, original-source rereads and later research comparisons found no supported separate active-parameter count for original T5-Large. Google’s Bikel table supplies counts only for 3B/11B, not Large. BMCook’s 0.60GB activated model size is a precision-dependent attention/FFN byte proxy excluding embeddings; MoEfication measures neuron-output sparsity and altered routed models. AltUp adds structural changes. Flan-Large’s active lead belongs to a gated-GELU, untied-embedding architecture rather than this original checkpoint. GPT-3 Appendix D’s half-active fraction remains approximate training-FLOP accounting. Keep null rather than converting byte sizes, percentages, or sibling conventions into a whole-model count.

architecture.note: Dense encoder-decoder Transformer: 24 layers per stack, bidirectional encoder attention, causal decoder attention and encoder-decoder cross-attention. ReLU feed-forward layers; relative position bias; no routed experts.

context_window.note: No fixed maximum-context ceiling is established. The 512-token value is a training/default sequence length. Relative-position bucket saturation at distance 128 is not a length cap; do not claim unlimited practical context either.

modalities.note: Text-to-text task inputs and outputs; no multimodal encoder or decoder in the original model.

reasoning.note: General NLP and reasoning-related benchmark tasks do not establish a dedicated thinking/reasoning mode in this original checkpoint. Later rationale-distilled derivatives do not verify the capability for it.

tool_call.note: No source-reported tool/function-calling capability for the exact original model was verified. Lack of documentation is not an explicit negative capability claim.

description.value: Google's original dense T5 encoder-decoder model for text-to-text tasks.
description.note: Plain description of the original architecture and task format without claims from later instruction-tuned variants.

Original Google T5-Large TensorFlow checkpoint index

patch.notes: The original checkpoint has 737,668,096 unique parameters across encoder, decoder and shared embeddings; Google’s 770M label is nominal. Tied embeddings count once; optimizer state and an unused 512-value conversion bias are excluded. No separate active-parameter count was found in the checked primary sources. A 512-token training/default length does not establish a fixed maximum context. Release date follows the original checkpoint release README and paper.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the verified 0.737668096B original T5-Large total and freshly confirms Google’s nominal 770M label. Explicit active null remains after checking later original research: byte-size proxies, neuron sparsity, structurally changed variants and unlisted sibling comparisons do not establish an applicable count. All twelve nonparameter assessments are unchanged. No weights or repeated tensor census.
